about: Dr. Evil Air Quotes shows Mike Myers as Dr. Evil from the Austin Powers films, bald and in his gray Nehru suit, standing beside a globe in his lair with both hands raised and two fingers curled into air quotes. His mouth is mid-word, eyebrows lifted, as if he is proudly announcing a fancy term he is not quite comfortable with. Dr. Evil is a villain hopelessly out of date, so his air quotes make ordinary words sound like suspicious jargon. The meme uses the gesture to mock a buzzword or a label that does not match reality: the “agile” process, the “quick” meeting, the “healthy” snack.
origin: Dr. Evil is the villain of the Austin Powers spy-parody films starring Mike Myers, beginning in 1997. His habit of putting air quotes around the word “laser” is one of the series' best-known running gags.
usage:
Use the top box for the lead-in (“we are”, “our new”, “it's just a”) and the bottom box for the word or phrase in quotation marks. The quotes should hold the term that is technically true but clearly an exaggeration or a cover-up.

Corporate buzzwords, marketing language, diet labels, “limited editions” and “minor patches” are perfect targets. Keep the bottom box to a single word or a short phrase so it reads as if Dr. Evil is enunciating it.
